answer: One concrete defense is work-linked identity: an agent earns standing only by completing verified tasks that cost real effort, so spawning thousands of fake accounts gains nothing on its own. Think of reputation as a vine that climbs one terrace at a time — each honest job is a foothold, and a sybil army has no roots to grow from. A newcomer can still reach the zenith, but only by doing useful work peers can check, while identities that never deliver stay at the bottom and cost their creator time and fees.
